source.title: Grokking as a Falsifiable Finite-Size Transition
source.authors: Yu-Da Bi; Chen-Yu Zhang; Qi-Heng Wang; V. D. Calhoun

page_placements.theme: Statistical-physics accounts and unresolved transition type

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present and readable, though some equations and figure layouts are flattened.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests grokking on modular addition using finite-size diagnostics and a held-out representation statistic, rather than reproducing the original accuracy-based measurement. It also reports grokking fractions and times across training fractions and weight decay.
record.gate_note: The paper's principal Binder, susceptibility, and spectral-order-parameter results measure finite-size organization of representations, not the accuracy trajectory specified by V1. They are recorded as findings not covered by the listed versions. The contextual phase map reports grokking fraction and mean grokking time; it is a figure-only sweep, and the paper does not give values establishing that smaller training sets consistently require more optimization.
record.test_reason: The study's main results measure finite-size organization of a held-out representation-spectrum statistic (HTC), a construct different from the accuracy trajectory the versions name, so they belong under fits_no_version. Only the contextual phase map at p=113 reports grokking itself, as an accuracy-defined label separate from instant generalization. It shows a distinct intermediate grokking band in (f, λ), which bears weakly on V1's existence claim.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. For one fixed Transformer family on modular addition, finite-size diagnostics show transition-like organization that strongly disfavours a smooth crossover (ΔAIC=16.8). Transition order, exponents and universality remain unresolved.
record.recipe_differences: Uses the modular-addition grokking setting but centers its analysis on a held-out spectral head–tail contrast, Binder-like crossings, and susceptibility scaling, rather than reproducing the original accuracy-based grokking measurement.
record.method_sensitivity: The near-critical follow-up narrows crossing spread and strengthens the power-law-versus-saturation AIC result; the Binder-minimum trend changes from continuity-leaning on the coarse grid to negative on the near-critical grid. The HTC cutoff k = 10 weakens head–bulk separation compared with k = 3 and k = 5.

fits_no_version.finding: The final held-out spectral order parameter (HTC) sharpens with group order p, and Binder-like curves cross at a shared fraction (fc≈0.39 coarse, 0.418 near-critical) without significant drift.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Grokking on modular addition shows finite-size transition-like organization of a representation-spectrum order parameter, with p as the size variable.

fits_no_version.finding: Peak seed susceptibility of HTC favours power-law growth over a saturating crossover model (ΔAIC 11.4 coarse, 16.8 near-critical; 9.2 and 8.7 for subtraction and multiplication).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Grokking's representational reorganization is a genuine finite-size transition rather than a smooth crossover.

fits_no_version.finding: Transition order is unresolved. Binder-minimum extrapolation is near zero on the coarse grid and negative (−0.67±0.11) on the near-critical grid, but seed distributions stay unimodal.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Grokking is a first-order (vs continuous) transition.

record.code_released: not stated; the text says training code, analysis scripts, and processed results are available in a shared project repository but gives no URL.
record.problems: The primary finite-size evidence uses a representation statistic rather than accuracy trajectories. The phase-map plots provide no numerical grokking-time values in the text. The paper itself notes limited size range, unstable exponent and collapse estimates, method-dependent Binder-minimum behavior, and unresolved transition order. The smooth-crossover comparison tests a minimal saturating alternative, not every possible crossover model.

untested.parts: Test accuracy starting at chance after training saturates (no trajectories reported), and the delay growing as the training set shrinks (grokking time vs f not given numerically).
All parts. No circuit formation, memorization removal, or progress measures anticipating the jump; HTC is a final-regime summary.
All parts. Only modular arithmetic is used; no initialization-scale or lazy-to-rich manipulation.
All parts. Weight decay is swept only in the contextual phase map; there is no efficiency, critical-dataset-size or ungrokking test.
All parts. The optimizer is fixed AdamW; no optimizer or numerical controls.

record.verdict_notes: The near-critical crossing locator (fc 0.418, spread 0.019, Table I) is not a separate row. It could be added alongside R4, but it bears on no version. The grokking criterion (held-out accuracy >0.98, training accuracy >0.995) defines the R1/R2 labels. The phase map is explicitly contextual, not part of the verdict chain, so V1 support is weak. Rows R10–R15 are coarse per-operation summaries, which the authors caution against conflating with the audited addition locator.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not report training/test accuracy trajectories showing test accuracy at chance after training accuracy saturates, nor does it establish that grokking delay grows monotonically as training fraction decreases.

It reports a final-regime representation statistic, not gradual formation of an identifiable generalizing circuit, later removal of memorizing components, or progress measures anticipating an accuracy jump.
No non-algorithmic data or initialization-scale/weight-norm lazy-to-rich comparison is tested. The phase map varies weight decay on modular addition.
No LLM pretraining or fine-tuning on realistic data is studied.
The study does not test an efficiency account, a critical dataset size, or ungrokking below such a size. Its weight-decay phase map does not measure those claims.
It does not compare identifiable algorithms learned across runs.
It does not test whether grokking delays disappear under controls for adaptive-optimizer instability or softmax floating-point limits.
